rv.q: There you have it, I thought to myself as I sat there Friday night at a play that every theater person, or broader creative professional, really should try and see.

Writer Stull and director Verdin have created a fully realized, haunting depiction of a future when exponential improvements in computer intelligence and technology will essentially and permanently change human society.
“The Singularity Play” is a timely and compelling show, if not a particularly hopeful one.
This is a thought provoking evening of theater in a lovely venue.
Overall, “The Singularity Play” is a thought-provoking piece that deftly handles complex themes with emotional intelligence and artistic flair.

cn.t: Critics praise this timely AI thriller as both disturbing and empathetic, with strong performances elevating Jay Stull's compelling exploration of artificial intelligence's unsettling intersection with human emotion and creativity.
